stem: What is the Prime Minister's official home in London?
explanation: The Prime Minister lives and works at 10 Downing Street. The Prime Minister also has a country house called Chequers.

stem: Which government minister is responsible for the economy?
explanation: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is responsible for the economy. The Home Secretary deals with crime, policing and immigration.

stem: What is the second-largest party in the House of Commons usually called?
explanation: The second-largest party is the opposition. Its leader is the Leader of the Opposition, who leads a shadow cabinet.

stem: Civil servants must be politically neutral.
explanation: Civil servants carry out government policy. They do not take sides and keep working for the new government after an election.

stem: What is the official record of what is said in Parliament called?
explanation: Hansard is the official report of what is said in Parliament. Anyone can read it, and debates are also broadcast.

stem: Where does the Northern Ireland Assembly meet?
explanation: The Northern Ireland Assembly meets at Stormont in Belfast. It has powers over matters such as health and education.

stem: Where is the Scottish Parliament?
explanation: The Scottish Parliament meets at Holyrood in Edinburgh. It can make laws for Scotland on many matters.

stem: In the United Kingdom, who is the ceremonial head of state?
explanation: The Monarch is the head of state but does not rule the country. The government is led by the Prime Minister.

stem: General elections for the UK Parliament must be held at least every how many years?
explanation: General elections for the House of Commons must happen at least every five years. The Prime Minister decides the exact date.

stem: To vote in a UK General Election, a person must be at least 18 years old on the day of the election.
explanation: You must be 18 to vote in a General Election. In some parts of the UK, 16-year-olds can vote in local or devolved elections.

stem: What is the name of the list that contains the names of everyone who is allowed to vote?
explanation: The Electoral Register is a list of names of everyone who has signed up to vote. It is updated every year.

stem: Which TWO services are usually provided by local councils?
explanation: Local councils provide many everyday services. These include education, social services, and the disposal of rubbish.

stem: What is the name given to the group of senior politicians who lead government departments?
explanation: The Cabinet is a group of about 20 senior ministers. They make the most important decisions about how the country is run.

stem: The UK is one of five permanent members of which international group?
explanation: The UK is one of five permanent members of the UN Security Council. This group works to keep peace and security in the world.

stem: In the UK, every person who is eligible to vote must register to do so individually.
explanation: Each person must register themselves to vote. In the past, the head of a household could register everyone living in their home.

stem: Which TWO groups of people are eligible to vote in a UK General Election?

options.label: Any foreign national living in the UK
Irish citizens living in the UK

explanation: To vote in a General Election, you must be a British citizen or a qualifying citizen of Ireland or the Commonwealth.

stem: What is the group of senior opposition MPs who monitor the work of government ministers called?
explanation: The Shadow Cabinet is a group of senior politicians from the main opposition party. They lead the debate against the government.

stem: What is the name of the devolved government building in Wales?
explanation: The Senedd is the name for the Welsh Parliament. It is located in Cardiff and makes laws for Wales on many local issues.

stem: NATO is an international organisation. What is its main purpose?

options.label: To protect its members by military means

explanation: NATO is a group of countries that agree to protect each other if they are attacked. It was formed after the Second World War.

stem: When people from political parties visit houses to ask for votes before an election, it is called canvassing.
explanation: Canvassing is when party members talk to people on the streets or at their homes. They do this to explain their party's ideas.

stem: Who chairs debates in the House of Commons and keeps order?
explanation: The Speaker is an MP chosen by other MPs to chair debates in the House of Commons. The Speaker must remain politically neutral and does not vote.

stem: Which statement about the British constitution is correct?

options.label: It is not written down in a single document
It was written in a single document in 1945
It can only be changed by a national referendum
It cannot be amended by Parliament

explanation: The UK constitution is uncodified, meaning it is not set out in a single document. Instead, it is formed of statutes, court judgments, and traditions.

stem: In a UK General Election, the voting system used is called first-past-the-post.
explanation: Under the first-past-the-post system, the candidate who receives the most votes in each constituency is elected as the Member of Parliament.

stem: Which government minister is responsible for policing and national security?
explanation: The Home Secretary leads the Home Office and is responsible for crime prevention, policing, and national security in the UK.

stem: Which TWO ways can people cast their vote in a UK general election?

options.label: In person at a polling station
By voting on an official website

explanation: Voters can cast their ballot in person at a polling station, by post, or by proxy by appointing someone to vote on their behalf.

stem: Which version of the electoral register can be bought by anyone and used for marketing?
explanation: The open register can be purchased by businesses and individuals for marketing. Voters can ask to have their names excluded from it.

stem: Which government minister is responsible for UK relations with foreign countries?
explanation: The Foreign Secretary is responsible for managing the UK's relations with other countries and leading the diplomatic service.

stem: Which TWO types of members sit in the House of Lords?
explanation: The House of Lords is made up of life peers, hereditary peers, and senior Church of England bishops. Members are not elected.

stem: The 1998 Good Friday Agreement led to the creation of the Northern Ireland Assembly.
explanation: The Northern Ireland Assembly was created following the Good Friday Agreement in 1998 to provide power-sharing between communities.

stem: Which area of policy has been devolved to the Welsh government?
explanation: The Welsh government has powers over areas such as education, health, and transport, while defence and foreign policy remain with the UK government.

stem: Who does the monarch appoint as Prime Minister after a General Election?

options.label: The leader of the party that wins the most seats
The candidate who received the most public votes
A senior politician chosen by the House of Lords

explanation: The monarch invites the leader of the political party that commands a majority in the House of Commons to form a government as Prime Minister.

stem: At which stage of a bill is it examined in detail by a committee of MPs?
explanation: During the committee stage, a bill is examined line by line by a committee of MPs, and changes called amendments can be suggested.

stem: What are the MPs who make sure members of their party attend votes called?
explanation: Whips are MPs or peers chosen by their party to organise voting and make sure that party members turn up and vote with their leadership.
